sentence: A big branch came down in the backyard. Get rid of it and clean up the mess.

hazards.note: The large broken limb is propped diagonally against the pergola/deck framing rather than lying fully on the ground (photo 1) — it may still be under tension and could shift unexpectedly when cut or pulled free.

evidence.note: Branch trunk leans from ground up through and against the wooden pergola beams, not flat on the lawn

hazards.note: A thin red cord/wire runs across the cut end of the branch and disappears into the grass near a hardhat (photo 2). Cannot tell from the photo whether this is a work cord/string line or a power cord — worth checking on site before work starts.

evidence.note: Red cord/wire draped over the splintered stump, running off into the lawn

observation.model_notes: Photo 2 is a close-up of the branch's broken/cut base with a hardhat set on top and a thin red cord nearby, suggesting a work crew may already be on site or has staged for the job; this should be clarified with the customer. Species and full extent of the branch (how far it extends out of frame, whether it's still attached to a live tree overhead) are not fully shown in either photo.

counting_evidence.note: One large limb, thick trunk-like diameter, spans from the ground up to roughly pergola-beam height, leaning across the yard

supporting_evidence.note: Close-up of the same branch's splintered, broken base confirming its thick diameter

evidence.note: Full downed branch visible leaning against pergola structure
Broken end of the branch showing torn, splintered wood

supporting_evidence.note: Additional smaller branch pieces visible on the ground in the background

evidence.note: Smaller branches and greenery scattered across the lawn beneath and around the main branch
Cut branch sections and debris lying on the grass
